activation.note: Activation covers all hierarchy artifact writes, including acceptance criteria, rather than only containment-field changes or existing findings. The change observer is explicitly targeting information, not an extra activation gate. Artifact kind and operation are directly observable; diff interpretation, validator findings and rollout phase honestly require observers. Phase controls strictness rather than whether traceability applies. The non-firing example excludes only changes outside planning artifacts.

audit.summary: All 18 segments survive at their claimed destinations, including containment fields, per-level validator assignments, rollout strictness and provenance. The additional full-chain checking procedure, phase-unknown handling and placeholder anti-pattern are declared additions; the single end-to-end traceability obligation has no new waivers, application-specific examples or shared-node displacement.

segmentChecks.note: The end-to-end Train -> Wagon -> Feature -> WMBT -> Acceptance chain and validator guarding are explicit in then; why adds the test-criteria endpoint without breaking the chain.
Phase 2 (PLANNER_TESTER_ENFORCEMENT) is stated as the point at which validators become strict and findings block, without inventing pre-Phase-2 strictness.
The level-to-containment-and-validator model is retained by the chain obligation and per-level instructions.
Wagons must be registered in a train's participants, with COVERAGE-PLAN-2.1 retained.
Features must be listed in their wagon's features[], retaining validator references 2.1 and 2.2.
WMBTs must be listed in their feature's wmbts[], retaining validator references 2.2 and 2.3.
WMBT acceptance links through acceptances[] are mandatory, with references 2.3 and 2.4 retained.
Acceptance test criteria are required in then and prefer, and the 2.4 validator reference is retained.

risks: No concrete validator command or project-specific mechanism for discovering the rollout phase is supplied; the planner must locate that tooling and must follow the explicit instruction to report an unknown phase rather than assume findings are advisory.

unobservable: Diff-level changes to participants, features[], wmbts[], acceptances[], or acceptance test criteria require the declared change observer.
Coverage validator findings require an observer that surfaces validator results.
The active PLANNER_TESTER_ENFORCEMENT rollout phase requires a phase observer.

review.summary: All knowledge-rich segments retain their hierarchy, field names, validator assignments, and rollout semantics at usable destinations. The coder-facing instructions give a deterministic end-to-end check for planning-artifact changes; only project-specific validator and phase discovery remain external, as the activation facts honestly declare.
